children: Dream Unlimited intends to renew its share-repurchase program to buy back up to 10% of its shares over the course of a one-year period.

The Canadian real estate developer on Monday said that the Toronto Stock Exchange accepted its plan to renew its normal course issuer bid to buy back up to about 2.38 million of its shares for cancellation.
Shares have been under pressure in 2026, falling about 11% to close Friday at 17.12 Canadian dollars (US$12.24).
At Friday's closing price, the value of the shares intended for buyback would be worth about C$40.7 million.
Dream can begin buying back shares starting Sept. 23.
